title: The Night Train
subtitle: The train chugs along, leaving no stragglers behind.

items.text: Classroom, Rayashki
As the chalk marks its final stroke, the lecturer exhales a long breath.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Class is over.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Thank goodness, I still remembered the basic premises of "Ley Lines and Biology."

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Feel free to ask me any questions.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Cheer up, little ones. There won't be any exams for this subject.
She offers a hesitant joke to ease the awkwardness of the class.
But their usual playful responses never emerge.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Mm?
She turns to face a class that must be bored, asleep, maybe distracted. She's met instead by clear and focused eyes.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Ms. Windsong, are you going to dig up those potatoes alone again?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Is there anything we can do to help you?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Vila said we will work together to beat the critters out there.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: That we will find their weakness as long as we finish the map with you!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Just like how you taught us to!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: "Qiqirn are not dangerous at all. They are plant-eating critters and pose little threat to humans."

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I have ropes, flowers, and white gloves. We will dig up a lot of potatoes together.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Pyotr is strong. He can move any rocks that are in our way. Nina can prepare a kettle of warm water for everyone. And ...
The children's voices rise and fall. What began as icy determination soon melts into a cascade of sobbing tears.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I'm sorry, little ones.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I wish I could verify all the theories we've been working on, but ...
She affixes Rayashki's ley energy map to the blackboard, circling an empty void.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: As you can see, a critical part is missing.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It might take months to finish it.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Besides, there may be even more dangerous critters in that area.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Then the town will become the witch's new castle? Or perhaps an empty castle.
Her attempt to turn the mood again falls flat.
A merciful bell rings out the dreary topic like a dirge.
Thankfully, the next teacher arrives swiftly to relieve her.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Quiet, children.
She holds her gaze firm, sweeping over the assembled children.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Wipe your tears and cheer up! Our Rayashki will stand strong!

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: Really?!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But what are you going to do?
Windsong is taken aback at first. Then, contemplating the possibilities, she delicately weighs her words.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Vila, I hope you aren't seriously considering Zeno's ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Of course not. They might try, but we will never give in!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: No matter what, for now, we must find a way to protect our town. We will need a shelter from these critters.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We've all decided to stay.
The curtains part, and sunlight pours in from outside.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Look outside, children.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Each and every one of us is doing what we can to hold our town together.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Knut's factory is spitting out puffy bubbles.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Heh heh.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The workers are going to transform the abandoned factories into something useful.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They are cleaning the ore and debris there. Not an easy job.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: After that, we will start new production lines and cooperate with the surrounding cities. We will grow potatoes, breed fish, and make canned food. We will find our strengths together!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Are we putting makeup on the factories? We can paint their faces and put beautiful garlands on them!

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Hmm? So what is Mr. Patrik doing?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Everyone's waiting in line. Is it the tin-hat festival again?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm sorry, Avgust. I think we will have to live without our tin hats and Comrade Blinchik for a long time.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They are signing on to a reform of our rationing.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: To transform our factories, we need to cut down the budget for the canteen.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Oh, thank you for your sacrifice, Comrade Blinchik.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: You deserve a medal and some chocolate!

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Look, the bulldozers are tearing down those houses!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Yes. We all agreed to exchange some of our living space.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: For more land to grow food.
The children crowd the window, silent but beaming with pride, as if paying tribute.
Windsong follows Vila's narrative to its conclusion.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The price is much higher than it first seemed. Is it worth it?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You cannot find what we have here in Zeno's barracks, or in a relief camp. You can't find it anywhere in the world.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Think about the old comrades and the babies. They are the past and the future of Rayashki. How could we leave them behind or subject them to Zeno's whims?
Mechanical sounds from outside carry across the snow from afar, as if the land itself is calling.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: No one shall ever be abandoned in Rayashki.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I think people out there would be envious if they saw what you are doing here.
She doesn't press further.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We really aren't doing anything so special. We're only doing our job, our duty to one another.
Her scales and spines have risen, though whether it's a sign of pride or fear, she can't say.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: There are lots of conflicts out there, conflicts like the one between humans and Rusalki.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Like the ones that mocked the study of ley lines and dissolved our school. They did so simply because it might take from their funds or steal their glory.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Everyone forever building walls, just to keep separated from each other—Hoarding whatever they could get their hands on.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Then they blame the aftermath—the harm they do to others on "cruel realities."

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Heh, "cruel reality." It seems to be everyone's mortal enemy, the cause of all suffering, war, greed—the perfect excuse to never care.
Her voice trails into a mutter.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But things are different in Rayashki.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They took me in unconditionally when I came here. And they stayed friendly for a week, a month, a year, and even now.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: So naturally, it became my dream, too.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Everyone here shares a beautiful dream, a dream that we can work and enjoy life together.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That someday there will be no more conflicts between people or worries about tomorrow. That everyone will be able to work to achieve their passions whatever field they wish to pursue. A utopia.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It's not just a way of life for now, but the future we're always trying to reach.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I've spread the study of ley lines in Rayashki, along with its potential.
A simple invitation catches Windsong's eye, with dense, messy signatures filling every possible space.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They showed great interest. The study tells us about the secrets that could lie beneath the earth, after all.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "Perhaps it will bring hope to Rayashki."

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But, I'm not one of you.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You taught the children something new, and you helped us explore our town's potential, didn't you?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Everyone here is more than happy to help you. You know, Comrade Knut has been boasting about the assistance he was able to provide for your studies.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: And many others are envious. They want to help you, too.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: More importantly, you already have a group of curious students here willing to study your theory.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Now, allow me to ask you again, Comrade Windsong.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Would you hold a lecture on ley lines for all the citizens of Rayashki?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Even though my research doesn't have any endorsements or achievements?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Of course. Perhaps we can be the first to endorse it, after your lecture.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You're being far too obvious in your recruitment tactics.
Vila smiles, ignoring her feigned protest.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The world is not a beautiful place. Poverty, privilege, egoism, exclusivism, so many problems.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But that doesn't mean it can't get better in the future.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Perhaps, the experiment we're doing in Rayashki now will become the symbol of a better future, a new world where all races and ideas can coexist.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Well, of course, it may fail and end up a ruin.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But at least we've tried.
She watches Vila standing proudly, as if gazing at a great ship bound for distant shores.
Venturing all, never shrinking back.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We love our home, and we're ready to devote our lives to it.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I can't shake the feeling you're inviting me aboard a leaky boat that could sink any moment.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Maybe, Comrade Windsong. But should we sink, remember your friend is a Rusalka, and we do well underwater.
Windsong blinks, half-wondering if her new friend has gone mad.
And finding it madder still that she is reaching out to solemnly accept the invitation.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: What an honor.
